stage.description: Factory, builder, prototype, and singleton patterns in PHP.

payload.markdown: Notice that the creator classes mirror the product hierarchy. This is a common consequence of the Factory Method pattern and disliked by some as a special kind of code duplication. Another issue is the possibility that the pattern could encourage unnecessary subclassing. If your only reason for subclassing a creator is to deploy the Factory Method pattern, you may need to think again (that’s why I introduced the header and footer constraints to the example here).

payload.markdown: I have focused only on appointments in my example. If I extend it somewhat to include to-do items and contacts, I face a new problem. I need a structure that will handle sets of related implementations at one time. The Factory Method pattern is often used with the Abstract Factory pattern, as you will see in the next section.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Include & Require: Loading PHP files at runtime; require_once guards against re-declaration.
Pattern Principles: What design patterns are, how to describe them, and when one fits.
Strategy Pattern: Swapping an algorithm behind a common interface at runtime.
UML Class & Sequence: Standard diagrams for static structure and runtime interaction.
